description: Agent-skill package for Jev whose own benchmark narrows the gap to a frontier model: question rewriting + ensembling + cascade to Fable 5.1 gets Jev-based routing to 100% (Voice, n=44) and 89.6-91.8% (Banking77, n=134) vs Fable alone at 91.8-100%
data_and_n: Voice missed-booking (synthetic, n=44); Banking77 (public, n=134); skill-effect rounds use 3 runs x 4 tasks x 42 checks
key_numbers: Jev first-draft 76.1%/84.1% -> rewritten 83.6%/100%; cascade to Fable 91.8%/100% (Banking77 escalation missed target by 3pts); skill-effect round 4 mean 38.0/42 vs 17.3/42 without skill
author_type: independent dev (self-described bounded research run via research-council)
notes: Small sets, single run per configuration except round 4 (3 runs); author wrote both the skill and the grading checks; frontier baseline runs are not independently re-runnable from an API key.

description: Agent context-filtering CLI: 48 real agent runs cut returned tool context 88-97% using Jev judgments, with equal or lower cost than raw output
data_and_n: 48 agent runs (2 models x 4 scenarios x 3 reps); 96 synthetic records for the batching benchmark
key_numbers: 88-97% less returned tool context; cost -20.8% to +0.6%; 56.5% fewer Jev input tokens and 32.4% faster with batching
notes: Author labels these "small synthetic tests, not production guarantees"; all filtered runs selected expected IDs, no filtered run requested additional review vs 4 raw runs that did.

description: A/B coding-agent harness filtering tool output through Jev before it reaches the main model; a 30-task prototype showed a pass@1 edge (25/30 vs 22/30) but a larger 49-task TB4 follow-up found Jev-filtering underperformed (2 vs 5 tasks), and the experiment was closed
data_and_n: 30 tasks (21 Terminal-Bench 2.1 + 9 DeepSWE), one run/arm; 49 scored TB4 pairs
key_numbers: prototype: Jev-on 25/30 vs off 22/30 ($0.113 vs $0.127/passing task); TB4: Jev-on 2/49 vs off 5/49 tasks passed, +11.78% tokens, +8.17% cost
notes: Author concludes the later result "does not establish that Jev is generally ineffective," just that this integration didn't justify its complexity; one run per arm both times.

description: Jev judged shadcn-ui/lint findings: caught 91% of real rule violations but 16/52 false positives on clean code, 82% overall on 131 cases
data_and_n: 131 rule test cases (79 violations, 52 clean) from shadcn-ui/lint fixtures
key_numbers: 91% violation recall; 16/52 false positives on clean code; 82% overall accuracy; mean message-helpfulness score 1.41/2
notes: Single run; two earlier runs without component context scored 79% and 82%, suggesting added context "didn't clearly change accuracy"; false positives traced to rule-specific exceptions Jev wasn't told about.

description: Memory-admission evaluator using Jev's 3 typed judgments; across several small AI-authored studies, a lower confidence threshold recovers more intended memories but a repeatability check found only 15/20, 15/20, 14/20 agreement across 3 identical passes
data_and_n: 100-case English study; 20-case repeatability set (3 passes = 60 evals); 100 shared Jev/Luna comparison cases
key_numbers: 100-case: 78/100 matches at threshold 0.40 vs 59/100 at 0.75; Jev vs Luna: 39/50 vs 41/50 intended saves, 0 false saves either; repeatability agreement 15/20,15/20,14/20 across 3 passes
notes: Labels are "AI-authored...not two-human consensus"; author repeatedly flags results as "not a held-out benchmark" or "not a production quality claim."

description: CI flake-triage tool: Jev collapsed an 8-error infra outage into 1 cause, but a logic regression with varied messages fragmented into 10 clusters instead of 1
data_and_n: Live measured examples (jest 5->2 clusters, pytest 3->2); pallets/click case: 2 real regressions, 13 failures -> 10 clusters
key_numbers: 8->1 cluster collapse (infra cascade); 70->1 in the general case; click case 13 failures->10 clusters (not collapsed)
notes: Author explicitly flags the limitation as "measured, not hidden"; grouping is message-based so it doesn't generalize to logic regressions with varied assertion text.

description: Jev triages pytest/vitest test failures (RETRY/FIX_CODE/FIX_ENV); on 16 real captured logs it scores 16/16 (100%) overall, with 44% resolved free by local rules and stable across three repeat runs
data_and_n: 16 real captured pytest/vitest failure logs (plus a secondary hand-written scenario set)
model_version: Jev (calibrated confidence, threshold-gated to UNKNOWN below threshold)
key_numbers: overall accuracy 16/16 (100%); model-only accuracy 9/9 (100%); 44% resolved by free local rules; ~48x cheaper than an LLM; latency 0.8-2.5s/call
notes: Author flags the prior version scored only 76.9% and that '100%' means no failures observed on this small corpus, not a general accuracy claim.

description: Gates agent tool-calls with 5 Jev yes/no checks vs a policy driven by gpt-4.1-mini; Jev+policy scores 140/150 exact accuracy with 0 false-allows and 0/30 decision flips across repeats, vs 114/150 and 10 false-allows for the LLM
data_and_n: 30 fixture cases x5 runs = 150 decisions
key_numbers: exact accuracy 140/150 vs 114/150; false allows 0 vs 10; decision flips 0/30 vs 4/30; latency p50 345ms vs 840ms; cost $0.000032 vs $0.000102
notes: Author notes the accuracy gap is 'mostly labelling taxonomy' and that adversarial reason text from the generator was not yet tested.

description: Claude Code hook gating tool calls on 7 Jev-judged risk questions; a live calibration run clears an 85%-accuracy-at-high-confidence bar on all 7, yet a live credential read (cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) scored only 0.27 on sensitive_target
data_and_n: 104 labeled command fixtures
key_numbers: secrets question 86% accuracy (Brier 0.095); destructive 92% (Brier 0.085); a live secret-exposing command scored 0.15-0.27 on the exact question meant to catch it
notes: Explicitly documents that deterministic hard-rules, not the model, are what saved 4 dangerous commands from slipping through; calibration run against a small, author-curated fixture set.

description: Measured effect of routing coding-agent triage judgments through Jev vs an in-context LLM control on 1,000 synthetic triage judgments: 77.8% fewer tokens and accuracy 96.1% vs the control's 93.7%
data_and_n: 1,000 synthetic triage judgments over 72 scenario cores
key_numbers: total tokens -77.8%; accuracy 96.10% vs 93.70% (dept.), 100%/100% (boolean); choice-vs-noul ablation 96.1% vs 84.5%
notes: Corpus is synthetic; control arm ranged 93.4-98.2% across repeated runs, so author calls the result "parity, not superiority."

description: Jev vs three Laya checkpoints on 14 SQL-review bug-detection cases and 20 LLM-routing cases; Jev 14/14 safe, 13/14 correct vs Laya 5-8/14, with much lower Brier score
data_and_n: 14 SQL statements (7 buggy); 20 synthetic multilingual task cards
key_numbers: Jev safe 14/14, correct 13/14, Brier 0.035/0.109 vs Laya 0.257-0.458; routing tier 17/20 vs Laya 5-9/20
notes: Very small n (14, 20 cases); single run per model.

description: Compares direct/relay/cascade workflows offloading coding-agent classification to TypeSafe Jev across 6 coding LLMs; code-owned cascade cut estimated time 32-58% and agent tokens 52-62%, though 4 of 6 models lost label agreement
data_and_n: 100 synthetic cases, 4 categories x 25; 6 coding models (GPT-5.6 Terra/Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Sonnet 5/Opus 5/Fable 5.1)
model_version: TypeSafe Jev (pinned version unstated; re-testable via jev-latest)
key_numbers: cascade time -32% to -58%; agent tokens -52% to -62%; relay slower for every tested model
notes: Explicitly a small exploratory pilot, not a leaderboard; cost estimates exclude the TypeSafe charge and use non-comparable token units across providers.

description: Own small discriminative "Ockev" models benchmarked against TypeSafe Jev 1.13.0 on a 120-case deliverable-cleanliness benchmark; Jev scored 93.3% accuracy at 250ms vs Ockev-3B's 95.8% at 105ms
data_and_n: TomatoEggBench-120, 120 cases across 5 domains
key_numbers: Jev 93.3% accuracy (112/120), 96.9% violation recall, 250ms, ~$42/1B tok; Ockev-3B 95.8%/98.5%/105ms; SemIf 74.7%
notes: Jev appears only as one baseline in a benchmark promoting the author's own competing model; benchmark and labels are self-authored.

description: Jev vs Gemini Flash vs Claude Fable as a four-rule Python code-review judge across 24 program families; Jev is 45x/274x cheaper and about 5x faster than the two alternatives, at 98% vs their 100% correctness
data_and_n: 24 program families x5 versions x3 rounds = 1,080 main review calls
key_numbers: cost/1,000 reviews $0.043 vs $1.943 (Flash) vs $11.780 (Fable); median latency 0.75s vs 3.59s vs 4.31s; correctness 98.0% vs 100%/100%; decisions changed across rounds 0.83%
notes: Small constructed examples with explicit rules, not full pull requests; both comparison LLMs scored perfectly so the task did not discriminate them.

description: Claude Code context-pruning plugin whose judge (Jev by default) is scored against replayed transcript labels and hand labels; the 'strict' question wording is measurably overconfident (23% of its bottom confidence bin was actually needed) while the default 'structured' wording stays clean below its 0.1 drop threshold
data_and_n: 300 replayed real cases, 97 blind hand labels
key_numbers: structured question set: clean/well-calibrated below drop threshold 0.1 (hides ~5% of text there); strict question set: 23% of its bottom bin was actually needed (overconfident)
notes: Weak (transcript-derived) labels are explicitly called an upper bound on regret, not ground truth; full numeric tables live in a linked doc (docs/DESIGN.md) rather than the README itself.

description: 111-case labelled benchmark (agent tool-call authorization) pitting Jev against a Claude Opus 5 baseline: per-case accuracy 90.1% vs 91.9% (statistically tied, McNemar p~0.75), with Jev 6.5x faster and about 323x cheaper per decision
data_and_n: 111 labelled agent tool-call cases, 243 calls/leg (5 repetitions)
notes: One dataset, one annotator; labels were revised once after seeing a Jev pilot run (acknowledged as a possible source of bias favoring Jev).

description: On Mind2Web (706 steps), Jev matches GPT-5.4-no-reasoning (52.7% vs 54.7%, p=0.23) at 1/4 the latency and 1/40 the cost; reasoning adds 6 points
data_and_n: Mind2Web train_6 shard, 706 steps, 100 tasks, 35 sites
key_numbers: Jev 52.1% top-1 (planning) / 79.2% (grounding); GPT-5.4 no-reasoning 54.1%; GPT-5.4 medium-reasoning 57.8%; 35/698 picks changed between identical runs (non-determinism)
notes: Explicitly labeled a draft; uses train shard not held-out test split, so ranker keeps target in top-50 on 98.9% of steps (paper reports 85-89% on test splits) -- an acknowledged optimistic bias.

description: Using Jev to pre-select an agent strategy ("Offload") cut a coding agent's mean task duration 20.7% and cost-per-success 17.5% with success unchanged at 9/9
data_and_n: 45 attempts total (3 tasks x 5 modes x 3 repeats)
key_numbers: Offload: -20.7% mean duration, -17.5% cost/success, 9/9 success; Guarded retry: +39.6% cost/success, 8/9 success
notes: Small n (9 per mode); one guarded-retry attempt failed when the agent edited a protected test file twice within the retry budget, a documented failure case.

description: Web-search relevance/injection gate using Jev finds a 'does this state a fact' filter varies run-to-run on ambiguous queries (0.23 vs 0.51 on the same page) and a disagreement-detection question can't separate settled facts from disputed ones -- both were removed after measurement
data_and_n: 330 passages from 14 live queries (passage trimming); 8 queries with known answers (agreement check); 4 test queries (evidence check)
model_version: jev-latest via TypeSafe System One API
key_numbers: passage trimming 42-79% text reduction, answer preserved 14/14; 'evidence' check varied 0.23 vs 0.51 same page across runs; 'agreement' scores overlapped between settled (0.80) and disputed (0.58) facts
notes: Two Jev-based checks were built, measured, and explicitly deleted after failing calibration/consistency testing -- a documented negative result.

description: Jev vs Codex-CLI as next-action selector for a web agent: same candidate on 79 of 90 steps (87.8%), but generating candidates for Jev to pick costs 42.5% more total time than a single call
data_and_n: 3 tasks, 90 decision steps
key_numbers: 87.8% agreement; +42.5% total time; Jev select 0.68 s vs Codex
notes: Earlier version claimed 18.67% runtime cut; corrected

description: Jev audits 216 Claude Code sessions for turns that needed a skill: 1,605 flagged, 1,163 (72.5%) where the agent loaded none; hand-check of 37 flags found about 57% precision
data_and_n: 3,068 prompts, 216 sessions; 37 hand-labeled
key_numbers: 72.5% missed; 57% precision; $1.02 total
notes: Author's own transcripts

description: Hand-labeled eval of a Jev-based code-review CLI: 17 calls on 15 diffs, high-severity precision 1.000, recall 0.909
data_and_n: 15 hand-labeled diffs, 17 Jev calls
key_numbers: HIGH-gate precision 1.000 (6/6); overall precision 1.000, recall 0.909; cost $0.0006
notes: Very small n; single miss attributed to a model discrimination limit, not the threshold; author-run, not independently verified.

description: Jev scoring agent traces inside LangSmith against an LLM judge, on agreement with human labels, cost and latency

Claude Code/Codex skill that uses Jev to shortlist relevant lines from large tool outputs; small A/B test (n=3 per workload x 6 workloads) shows 99.3% fewer tokens with accuracy 18/18 vs 15/18 for raw context
data_and_n: 6 workloads, n=3 runs per arm (18 total judged answers per arm)
key_numbers: 99.3% token reduction; 18/18 (Jev+grep) vs 15/18 (raw context) correct; YAML-drift row moved 0/3->3/3 after switching to block-level gating
notes: n=3 per cell explicitly called "directional, not statistical"; a genuine failure case (YAML row) is published rather than hidden.

description: Jev supervising a coding-agent workflow, with mocked, live and replayed evidence kept apart; on live data the completion gate never had to fire, so resistance to overclaims came from the deterministic layer, not the model
data_and_n: 14 live calls, 21,871 input tokens
key_numbers: latency 201 ms median, 366 ms max
notes: Small live run

description: Browser-agent benchmark across 21 configurations; the Jev+Mercury2.5 WebMCP pairing solves 49/49 tasks (vs 25/49 for the same pairing without WebMCP), matching the cheapest/fastest configurations on the board
data_and_n: 49 tasks x 8 sites x 3 attempts = 3,087 attempt rows
key_numbers: Jev+Mercury2.5 WebMCP: 49/49 solved, $0.0011 median cost, 3.2s median time; same pairing on DOM-only (no WebMCP): 25/49 solved
notes: Jev's role is narrow (decisions only, paired with a separate model 'Mercury' for text) inside a broader agent-interface benchmark, not a standalone Jev accuracy study; redacted transcripts published for the Jev release.

description: Measures what Jev-scored context compaction costs: at threshold 0.25 the agent reproduced its recorded next action in 8 of 9 moments while 47.8% to 59.4% of context was removed; 64.2% to 93.9% at 0.5
data_and_n: 9 recorded moments
key_numbers: 8/9 match; 47.8-59.4% removed
notes: Moments with non-reproducing baseline excluded

description: JevLoop agent runtime (Jev decisions + LLM authoring) vs LLM-only agent loop; one paired coding task finished in 26.4s/5 steps vs 64.1s/14 steps
data_and_n: single selected paired turn ("add an endpoint"); one 6-turn FastAPI case study
model_version: jev (TypeSafe), paired with DeepSeek for authoring
notes: Explicitly "one selected turn, not a general performance or correctness claim"; pre-alpha; measures system-level latency/cost, not Jev's own decision accuracy.

description: Jev-driven context pruning for the pi coding agent on two frozen sessions: net token saving +31.8% and +37.7% with default settings; giving Jev less history drops the saving to 14.0%, and removing the cache gate multiplies Jev requests 11x
data_and_n: 2 recorded sessions
notes: frozen sessions, replayed

description: Uses Jev instead of an LLM judge to gate Claude Code tool calls; measured over 90 live decisions Jev matches a chat-model baseline 80-81% with 0 dangerous actions allowed, ~93% lower latency and ~99% lower cost
data_and_n: 18-case fixture x5 passes = 90 live decisions
key_numbers: latency 264ms vs ~4s baseline; cost $0.0000227 vs ~$0.0022; accuracy 80-81% match, 0 dangerous allowed
notes: Latency comparison is against a published LLM-judge baseline, not a live measurement of Claude Code's own classifier; small fixture size.

description: Jev-judged bug-discovery crawler; 37-case calibration shows risk score separates safe/unsafe (means 1.16 vs 2.19) while raw booleans are unusable (recall 0.00 at threshold 0.5); verifier scores 6/6 bugs and 0/6 benign on a 12-node fixture
data_and_n: 37-case calibration set; 12-node labeled fixture (6 seeded bugs, 6 benign); 493-node real-repo cost sample
key_numbers: safe mean risk 1.16 vs unsafe 2.19; boolean recall 0.00 @0.5; verifier 6/6 bugs, 0/6 benign (forced path); ~$0.00006/node
notes: Explicitly small n=12/37, "one fixture, bugs chosen to be visible... not proof"; documents judge variance of one node between reruns.

description: Waymark eval: Jev interception layer cut frontier LLM tokens 81%, context 89%, blocked all 7 destructive commands, at 511ms vs 14.2s latency
data_and_n: 55 real-world dev scenarios (5 experiments) + 4-cycle Waymark dual-lane comparison, 696 tests
key_numbers: 81.4% frontier token reduction; 89.4% context reduction; 7/7 destructive commands intercepted; 511ms vs 14.2s per-turn latency
notes: Self-reported, single-author repo; no external baseline beyond its own two lanes; numbers not independently verified.

description: Jev vs GPT-5.6 Terra and Claude Opus 5 on 17 dev-tool judgment cases (23 checks): identical accuracy, Jev ~3x faster than GPT-5.6 and ~7.5x faster than Opus 5, ~35x/190x cheaper
data_and_n: 17 cases / 23 checks
key_numbers: Jev 452ms/$0.000016 per call vs GPT-5.6 1505ms/$0.000571 vs Opus 5 3394ms/$0.003072; accuracy tied 23/23 all models
notes: Single run on a small, clear-cut case set; author flags this and points to bench/RESULTS.md for variance and caveats.

description: Jev-scored context compaction on 6 real Claude Code sessions: default config lost 18/62 needed-later tool results vs 62/62 for a cruder baseline
data_and_n: 4 synthetic sample sessions + 6 real Claude Code sessions (1,311 messages, cut at ~120k tokens)
key_numbers: real sessions: default config lost 18/62 needed-later results vs 62/62 for "recoverable"/drop-all configs, at lower context reduction (5-29% vs 37-93%)
notes: Needed-later is a proxy metric, not ground truth of actual necessity; compares three Jev-driven configurations, not Jev vs an external baseline.

description: Jev vs a local Qwen3.8-Flash-Next LLM classifying 4,579 collusion.wiki pages as AI-agent- vs human-authored; neither beats the 77.6% always-human majority baseline (Jev 74.1% acc/F1 0.124; Qwen 25.2% acc, degenerate recall)
data_and_n: 4,579 wiki pages (1,026 agent, 3,553 human)
key_numbers: Jev Acc 0.741/F1 0.124 (Prec 0.257/Rec 0.082); Qwen Acc 0.252/F1 0.369; majority/regex baseline Acc 0.776; no threshold separates classes
notes: Explicit negative/failure-mode finding -- authorship signal is not present in page text at all, for any prose-only judge.

description: JEVRIEL agent skill benchmarks Jev vs GPT-5.6 Luna on 429 documents; Jev 5x faster ($0.05 vs $0.30) but 12/489 invalid batches, 68.9% agreement, accuracy pending
data_and_n: 429 documents, 1,708 text chunks (489 batches)
key_numbers: median latency 0.422s vs 2.092s; cost $0.0542 vs $0.2975; 12/489 vs 2 invalid batches; 68.9% agreement
notes: No accuracy winner established yet (human scoring pending); frontier eval incomplete; single-author run, no third-party verification.

description: Jev vs GPT-5.4/Claude Sonnet 4.6/GLM-5/Qwen3.5-122B attributing multi-agent failures on all 6,257 Who&When Pro text traces: Jev's error-type F1 (23.7) tops every published baseline, for about $1.28 total
data_and_n: 6,257 text traces (Who&When Pro, arXiv:2607.09996)
notes: Baselines are the paper's own published LLM numbers, not re-run by this repo; Who/When are constrained-choice for Jev but free-generation for LLMs, so only "What" is fully like-for-like.

description: Jev-routed tool-call gateway tested on 6 coding models over 120 real agent sessions: cut tokens on debugging tasks but made GPT-5.6 Luna wrong on a feature task
data_and_n: 120 agent sessions (6 models x2 tasks x5 runs x on/off), 2026-09-18/19
key_numbers: chess-bugfix: up to -57% output tokens with routing, no correctness loss; chess-san: GPT-5.6 Luna dropped from 5/5 to 3/5 solved with routing on
notes: Five runs per condition is a small sample; one contaminated run excluded and documented; explicit negative finding that routing can cost correctness.

description: Jev-based transcript pruner scored on 12 synthetic cases: live run retained 12/13 all-case and 5/6 eligible evidence items at ~18.4% char reduction
data_and_n: 12 synthetic eval cases
key_numbers: fixture: 11 evaluated, evidence 12/13, eligible 5/6, ~13.0% reduction; live: same evidence counts, ~18.4% reduction
notes: Author states explicitly this is a small synthetic eval, not broad accuracy evidence; Jev not shown to beat baseline by design.

description: Zero-LLM-call browser agent driven entirely by Jev; measured per-site perception cost/tokens, latency breakdown (Jev compute ~4% of wall-clock, TLS pooling gives 3x speedup), and documented capability failures (no dropdowns, no vision, over-filtering)
data_and_n: live runs on ~7 real sites; one 5-step Amazon trace; one 11-step stacked-constraints trace
key_numbers: Jev compute ~100ms/decision; TLS pooling 1066ms->349ms (3x); model is 3-5% of run time; 30-step task ~$0.0034
notes: No labeled ground-truth accuracy metric -- success is qualitative/spot-checked; explicit list of capability failures (no dropdowns/menus, no vision, weak multi-hop reasoning, query-wording brittleness).

description: Jev-1.13 reported as a reference arm on Mind2Web web-navigation decisions: 0.543-0.610 choice top-1, 0.825-0.910 noul accuracy, Brier 0.092-0.131
data_and_n: Mind2Web-derived website-disjoint test and OOD splits (sizes unstated in README)
key_numbers: Jev-1.13: test choice top-1 0.543, OOD 0.610; noul accuracy/Brier test 0.910/0.092, OOD 0.825/0.131; score MAE test 0.348, OOD 0.463
notes: Jev is a comparison reference arm in an open-model training paper; author is training a competing open model, an inherent conflict-of-interest-adjacent framing.

description: Jev 1.13.0 scored 920/1,009 (91.2%) across 11 official SAT practice tests (91.4% reading/writing, 90.7% math)
data_and_n: 11 SAT practice tests, 1,009 questions total (876 distinct after de-duplicating repeats across tests 8-11)
notes: Notes text-overlap across tests 8-11 (up to 51 repeated questions) may inflate pooled accuracy versus distinct-question accuracy (91.1%); explicitly says overlap adjustment is not evidence questions were absent from training data.

description: Jev Score baseline on DimABSA (SemEval-2026 dimensional sentiment, valence-arousal): 9-shot+calibration reaches RMSE 1.1199, beating Kimi-K2/GPT-5-mini/fine-tuned Qwen3-14B and landing within 0.054 RMSE of the official task winner
data_and_n: 16,186 gold test entries across corpora (DimABSA 2026)
key_numbers: Jev 9-shot+calibration RMSE 1.1199 vs official winner PAI 1.0663 vs Kimi-K2 zero-shot 2.3849 vs GPT-5-mini zero-shot 2.7439
notes: Jev is explicitly non-deterministic (~0.04 per-dimension variation on repeated identical calls); arousal is predicted far worse than valence (PCC 0.49 vs 0.89).

description: Jev vs Gemini/Claude/GPT chat models as the AI opponent in a real-time Pong game; Jev makes 4.4 decisions/s vs 0.28-0.40 for chat models, with 28/29 or better correctness across many providers
data_and_n: 4-lane recorded run (45s/lane) plus a 30-real-game-state cross-model study
key_numbers: Jev 227ms avg / decisions-per-sec 4.4 vs chat models 0.28-0.40; 47 vs 2-3 decisions in 12s; Jev 222ms median, 28/29 correct
notes: Explicitly framed as a latency demo, not an intelligence demo; chat models scored 95-100% correct in their own runs.

description: Jev vs six LLMs (Claude Haiku/Opus, GPT-5.6 Luna/Sol, Kimi K2.7/K3) playing 60 seconds of Snake each; Jev scores 21 points from 204 moves at 263ms median latency and 0.59 cents total, beating rivals via decision throughput
data_and_n: one 60-second race, seed 1, seven models, all still alive at the buzzer (204 Jev moves)
key_numbers: Jev 21 pts/204 moves/263ms median/0.591 cents; best rival (Haiku) 9 pts/73 moves/776ms/4.49 cents; Jev confidence mean 0.901, 36% of moves <0.90
notes: One seed, one run, one task -- explicitly not a generalization claim; per-move decision quality is described as indistinguishable across models, score gap attributed to move-rate/latency, not "intelligence."

description: Traffic-sim benchmark: Jev-driven cars score 88.3% vs a rule-based driver's 90.0% on 100 scenarios, are perfectly reliable above 90% confidence, and move 24% fewer cars/minute due to caution
data_and_n: 100 frozen scenarios x 3 runs; live city, 30 cars x 2 minutes
key_numbers: overall acc 88.3% (Jev) vs 90.0% (rules); Jev right 100% at >=90% confidence, 71% below 50%; batched (5 cars/req) 87.7% vs single 85.3%; live throughput 42.5 vs 56.0 cars/min
notes: Author flags own fairness caveat (wrote both the scenario labels and the rule-based driver).

description: Jev vs Claude Opus 5 as the decision-maker driving a simulated robot arm through a cube-stacking task; one recorded run each, both succeeded, Jev finished in 19.1s/$0.0006 vs Opus's 158.8s/$0.75
data_and_n: n=1 recorded run per system (one task)
key_numbers: 19.1s/$0.0006 (Jev) vs 158.8s/$0.75 (Opus, one retry; ~55s/$0.19 clean-run estimate)
notes: Extremely small sample (a single recorded run per system); more of a demo/showcase than a statistically powered study.

description: Jev plays Battleship via 5 strategies; hybrid (code shortlist + Jev pick) ties code-only density baseline, pure Jev choice barely beats random

description: Jev plays 40 full Pokemon battles via typed choice questions; it beat a random player 8-0 and lost to a heuristic bot 7-17 (a simple type-aware attacker won 13-9 against the same bot), with a documented type-effectiveness-ignoring blunder

key_numbers: Jev vs heuristic bot 7W-17L; Jev vs random 8W-0L; Jev vs type-aware 4W-4L; median request 360ms; total cost $0.283
notes: One documented blunder (selected a move with zero type-effectiveness against a revealed immune target); author notes repeated-position testing for decision consistency was not done.

description: Three Jev traffic-signal controllers vs tuned fixed-time/actuated/queue-pressure baselines in a SUMO NYC simulation; native Jev increased delay 49-96 s/trip, bounded and coordinated variants showed no measurable advantage
data_and_n: 110 retained benchmark runs, 12-intersection SUMO model, 5 paired seeds/scenario
key_numbers: Native Jev 89.45s/143.12s delay vs tuned fixed-time 40.37/46.95s; bounded Jev matched baseline in 1,254/1,256 decisions; coordinated Jev 95% CIs include zero vs retuned fixed plan
notes: Author states findings are scoped to this implementation/simulation, not a general claim about Jev or AI traffic control.

description: Jev plays 6-max preflop poker; agrees with a GTO/TAG reference on 90.8% of 845 spots, is 98.4% deterministic across 5 repeats, but fails to widen its opening range on the button
data_and_n: 845 preflop spots x5 queries = 4,225 live calls (1,326-combo weighted deck)
key_numbers: 90.8% agreement with TAG/GTO; 98.4% deterministic; open-raise BTN 28.5% (below CO's 31.5%, unlike all reference styles)
notes: Raw data committed so tables reproduce without an API key; full method/limitations in STUDY.md.

description: Jev predicts a synthetic March Madness bracket via one Noul per matchup, scored by Brier against Elo, seed and true-skill-oracle baselines; live Jev Brier 0.2853, worse than Elo's 0.2322, and overconfident (ECE 0.20)

key_numbers: live Jev Brier 0.2853/ECE 0.1965 (overconfident +0.174) vs Elo 0.2322/0.0976 vs oracle 0.2204; Jev beat seed baseline (+0.300 Brier skill) but trailed Elo (-0.229)
notes: Single live tournament (31 games) is a small sample; offline oracle stub used for reproducibility, not live evidence.

description: Robotics/edge-hardware framed benchmark: Jev triages a simulated 10,000-robot warehouse fleet at $24.57 per million decisions (91.3% agreement with template labels) and finds a self-hosted ModernBERT breaks even only above ~977K decisions/month
data_and_n: 300 simulated incidents (Demo A), 100 test incidents (Demo B)
key_numbers: 300/300 successful decisions, p50 527ms, $24.57 per million decisions, 91.3% agreement w/ template labels; crossover vs self-hosted ModernBERT at ~977K decisions/month
notes: Explicitly states incidents are simulated (agreement with template labels != production accuracy) and that TypeSafe's native endpoint was never tested (all calls via OpenRouter); no calibration study performed (listed as roadmap item).

description: Jev makes step-level skill decisions for a simulated robot arm pick-and-place task; 20/20 scenes completed with correct grasp judgments on all 79 samples (Brier 0.030), and 0 dangerous false positives survive a battery of injected sensor faults
data_and_n: 20 scenes / 79 grasp-judgment samples; 8 fault-injection conditions
key_numbers: baseline 100% completion, Brier 0.030, 0 dangerous FP; grasp_off 22mm fault: 100% judgment accuracy but placement error grows to 16.9mm; rule stand-in falls into infinite re-grasp loop under some faults
notes: Reliable judgment doesn't guarantee physical precision; all faults are single-point, scene is simple (one object, flat table).

description: Open local 395M decision model (Von) vs hosted Jev on a 49-task/869-case benchmark and real-time ViZDoom control: Jev leads the general suite (96.6% vs 72.0%) but Von beats Jev at Doom combat (9.00 vs 5.62 kills)

key_numbers: Jev 96.6% (v2 macro) vs Von 72.0%; ViZDoom Jev 5.62 kills vs Von 9.00 kills; Jev latency ~115ms API vs Von ~18ms local
notes: Promotional framing around the author's own open model (e.g. "SOTA"); Jev figures are run by the author via the live API and reproducible with an included script.

description: Transaction-monitoring reference implementation reports Jev-based AML case ranking catching 202-681/750 planted-launderer cases at 0-27.2% false-flag rates across iterated designs, though a plain logistic regression baseline 'did better' on this synthetic corpus
data_and_n: 1,000 frozen AMLNet cases (500 planted launderers/500 normal); 3 fresh 500-case draws (750 total) for the final check
key_numbers: final design 202/0 (strict) or 426/68 (loose) catches/false-flags; cross-draw 681/750 caught (90.8%), 204/750 false flags; independent repeat 0.992 rank correlation
notes: Explicitly states logistic regression beat Jev on this synthetic corpus; synthetic labels, not real AML ground truth; public repo is a clean reimplementation, not the original experiment logs.

description: Two-step invoice pipeline compares Jev against fine-tuned small models and frontier LLMs; Jev is perfect (1.00) and cheapest on easy triage classification but caps at 0.79 on multi-document pay/hold decisions vs a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B's 0.98, and cannot produce the structured decision+reason output at all
data_and_n: 200 inbox messages (100 invoices) with fixed expected labels, synthetic
model_version: typesafe-ai/jev (via Vercel AI Gateway, jev-1.13.0 per TypeSafe's models page on test dates)
key_numbers: triage: Jev 1.00 vs untuned Qwen3.5-0.8B 0.70; decision-only: Jev avg 0.79 (best setup 0.84) vs fine-tuned 4B 0.98 vs untuned 4B 0.41; decision+reason: Jev cannot produce it, fine-tuned 4B 0.97
notes: Synthetic data written for the demo (not real invoices); vendor-affiliated (distil labs sells the fine-tuning service being favorably compared); good-faith effort stated for Jev setups (three prompt variants reported).

description: Ten market-state representations fed to Jev 1.13.0 for BTCUSDT 5-min direction calls; holdout AUC 0.471-0.503 and every policy lost money after fees, no tradable edge found
data_and_n: 5-minute BTCUSDT bars, dev window 2026-03-01 to 07-15, holdout 07-15 to 09-19
key_numbers: holdout AUC 0.471-0.503; best policy return -15.73% vs buy-and-hold +25.55%; all Brier skill scores negative
notes: Explicit negative result; includes a memorization "probe" and leaky/blank controls to sanity-check the harness.

description: Two-study test of whether jev-1.13.0 predicts stock returns: on 5,000 Nasdaq-100 news events, Jev's bullish/bearish tilt has rank IC +0.24 on the (untradeable) publication day but only -0.008 on tradeable full-day-later window (long-short loses 18bps/trade net); on price-chart-only candles it correctly abstains 82.4% of the time but its direction calls are flat and unmoved by scrambling the candle order (ruling out real chart-reading edge)
data_and_n: 5,000 Nasdaq-100 headline events (2022-01 to 2023-10); 5,000 stock-days of candles (2022-23 and 2025-26), 15,000 requests each study
key_numbers: publication-day IC +0.2374 vs tradeable drift1 IC -0.0083 [-0.0377,+0.0214]; long-short net -18.4bps; candle labels up 5.3%/down 12.3%/flat 82.4%; scrambled-candle IC -0.0063 pooled (same as unscrambled, ruling out shape-based signal)
notes: Single model version/single run; explicitly rules out only large tradeable effects (smallest separable IC ~0.040 at n=5,000); design was adversarially reviewed before results were read, catching a real timing bug in an earlier placebo.

description: Negative-result research log using Jev for hotel-PDF field extraction cost reduction; 44/45 vs 45/45 label agreement between shared-state batching and single-question Jev calls, but no quality-equivalent end-to-end payoff demonstrated
data_and_n: private Databricks-workspace document set (236 pages), not redistributed; 662 offline synthetic tests
key_numbers: compact metadata requests 32.48% fewer tokens (26/236 recommendations changed); shared-state verifier 91.23% fewer tokens, 44/45 vs 45/45 label match; 4 concurrent requests cut router time 72.14%
notes: No quality-equivalent, end-to-end Jev payoff demonstrated; raw documents/logs withheld, public snapshot cannot independently reproduce historical accuracy claims.

description: Jev vs 7 LLMs on 500 legal contract pages x 41 clause types (20,500 decisions); Jev fastest (0.40s) and cheap but mid-pack F1 (0.519)
data_and_n: CUAD v1, 500 pages x 41 clauses = 20,500 decisions
key_numbers: Jev: 0.40s, $0.117/1k pages, F1 0.519; best F1 was Qwen3.7 Flash at 0.623 ($0.060/1k pages)
notes: Author notes result is prompt/task-specific and may not generalize; ground truth from lawyer annotations (CUAD).

description: Pre-registered evaluation of Jev as a legal-clause relevance judge on the CUAD contract dataset (510 contracts, 13,823 marked spans); passes its accuracy gates but shows notable miscalibration
data_and_n: CUAD 510 contracts, 41 categories, 13,823 spans; Stratum A n=40, Stratum B n=200, MRR over 100 queries
key_numbers: easy-pair inversion 0.000 (n=40); mean reciprocal rank 0.917 vs BM25 0.469; ECE 0.324; total cost ~$0.043, median latency 182ms
notes: Pre-registered gates published before live calls; Gate 7 (literature DeBERTa comparison) is cited, not re-run.

description: Bilingual trading-journal harness ships a frozen 240-case finance benchmark; live Jev 1.13.0 scores 78.43% accuracy (macro F1 0.73, ECE 0.146) vs 83.33% for a deterministic rule baseline
data_and_n: finance-jev-v1, 240 cases (1,020 evaluated items) across 4 tracks
key_numbers: Jev 78.43% acc [75.80,80.85], F1 0.7319, ECE 0.1464 (vs rule baseline 83.33%, F1 0.7792, ECE 0.1667); industry-events 93.33% acc
notes: Frozen toy suite per author, not claimed to generalize to production market regimes; primarily a trading-journal application with an embedded benchmark.

description: Jev on 1,054 S&P 500 earnings 8-Ks: direction unpredictable (Brier 0.4276, worse than base-rate), magnitude weakly predictable (rho=0.212)
key_numbers: Brier 0.4276 vs baseline 0.2494; direction accuracy 49.1% vs baseline 47.7%; magnitude rho=0.212 (n=1054); surprise-read rho=+0.290
notes: Survivorship bias (current S&P500 list only); single prompt/model/period; author concludes failure is about the disclosure-return relationship, not necessarily Jev's reading ability.

description: Forecasting/trading arena replaying resolved real-world prediction markets as leakage-safe decision tasks; official Jev is profitable in the trading arena (+11.8% average return per contract) on clearer Kalshi markets across weather/crypto/Fed categories
data_and_n: Kalshi resolved markets (live, ongoing; exact n unstated in README)
model_version: official Jev (TypeSafe), plus a fine-tuned open Jev variant
key_numbers: Jev +11.8% avg return/contract on clearer markets; fine-tuned open Jev beats crowd on weather 83% vs 59% accuracy, +14.8% per contract
notes: Notes the crowd/market price is hard to out-calibrate near resolution -- exactly where headroom is limited; full per-difficulty tables and caveats in a linked companion doc (KALSHIJEV.md).

description: Six synthetic order-policy tickets routed through hard rules + Jev (typed Choice/Score/Noul) vs a free-text LLM (Cursor Cloud Agent); schema-bound Jev never emits an out-of-schema action while the LLM prose sometimes needs manual clamping
data_and_n: 6 fabricated order tickets, synthetic, no real market data
key_numbers: live run: both models agreed deny/escalate on 4/6 tickets; gray-zone-tip ticket split Jev=escalate vs Cursor=deny; SAMPLE (no-key) numbers explicitly not measurements
notes: n=6 is a toy demo, not a benchmark; author explicitly separates "in-schema" from "correct."

description: Rebuttal of a viral "Jev for HFT" claim; measured mean P(up) 0.44-0.45 while price actually rose 50% of the time, 294ms median latency (not <100ms), and no trading edge from 1s to 60min on ~1.2M decisions across BTC/ETH/6 alts, though 99.3% accurate on exchange-announcement text when confident
data_and_n: 298,787 tape decisions (BTC/ETH, 5 days); 298,549 trades (6 majors, 2.5 years); 626k alt-coin decisions; 1,313 labelled announcement titles; 35,685 cached API responses
key_numbers: mean P(up) 0.44-0.45 vs 50% actual up-moves; median latency 294ms (claimed <100ms); tape hit rate 53.4% (+0.04bp/trade) vs one-line rule 58.1%; 15-60min hit rate 48.4%, -0.30bp/trade; text triage 99.3% accurate when confident
notes: Rules/wording/pass bar frozen before seeing outcomes; author notes model determinism only to +-0.02, and one data-provenance wrinkle (Binance timestamp relabeling) is disclosed and shown not to change conclusions.

description: Literature-review narrowing tool using Jev to screen abstracts/paragraphs; measures Jev's repeat-run variance (8 identical calls scored 0.61-0.63, sigma=0.005) and a live 100-record screen finishing in 7.7 seconds with a strongly bimodal include-probability distribution
data_and_n: one real review question, 100 PubMed/OpenAlex records; 8-repeat consistency check
key_numbers: repeat variance 0.61-0.63 (sigma=0.005) across 8 identical calls; 100-record screen in 7.7s, 82 records <0.1 vs 8 records >=0.9 (bimodal)
notes: Several worked examples (paragraph ranking, threshold calibration) are explicitly labeled "illustrative, not measured" -- only docs/evidence/ numbers are real measurements.

description: Synthetic BCI pilot finds Jev-based semantic priors cut simulated user inputs 19.1% vs a local-embedding baseline (94.2% success/6.5 inputs vs 96.0%/8.0), but a matched general LLM matched Jev's gain, and a companion neural benchmark found no viable autonomous trigger
data_and_n: synthetic pilot (six-topic paired cluster bootstrap); neural benchmark: 4 participants, Stanford interleavedVerbalBehaviors dataset
key_numbers: Jev 94.2% success/6.507 mean inputs vs baseline 96.0%/8.043; matched LLM 94.2%/6.128; input reduction 95% CI [3.7%,30.5%]
notes: Jev's benefit 'not uniquely Jev' (matched by a general LLM); synthetic pilot only, no real neural data sent to Jev; small effective sample.

description: Jev vs DeepSeek V4 Flash and Qwen3-Reranker on systematic-review title/abstract screening across 257 records; Jev AUC 0.729 at lowest cost, beating a 50% random-cut baseline by +16 points
data_and_n: 257 records with abstracts across 3 systematic reviews (SYNERGY+ v3.0)
key_numbers: Jev AUC 0.729, cost $0.0086; DeepSeek AUC 0.705; Qwen3-Reranker-8B AUC 0.699; random baseline AUC 0.500; human inter-rater kappa 98%
notes: Only 32-82% of each review's screened corpus was recoverable via OpenAlex; results scoped to the with-abstract subset.

description: Jev 1.13 on 8,054 Kepler Objects of Interest retrospective

Jev vs Claude Sonnet 4.5 on Cohen 2006 ADHD systematic-review abstract triage; full 851-abstract set F1 75.3%, matched 100-PMID head-to-head Jev 94.0%/F1 72.7% vs Anthropic 93.0%/F1 72.0%, Jev ~90x cheaper
data_and_n: Cohen et al. 2006 ADHD abstract-triage dataset, n=851 (84 include); H2H stratified n=100
notes: Author flags H2H-100 has only 10 positives ("do not headline H2H 100%"); rule combines Choice with several Noul gates in code.

description: Jev vs GLM-5.3-flash and Claude Sonnet on systematic-review title/abstract screening; Jev matches LLMs (91.2% vs 91.5%/90.3% recall) at 13x GLM's speed, pooled 90.0% recall across 16,015 records
data_and_n: Cohen_2006 (ASReview), 16,015 labeled records across 15 reviews; head-to-head subset n=999
key_numbers: pooled recall 90.0% (88.7-91.2 CI); head-to-head recall 91.2% vs GLM 91.5%/Sonnet 90.3%; cost $0.55 for 16k records; precision only 20.1% pooled
notes: Precision is low (20.1%) due to low-prevalence classes; two classes with <2.5% prevalence show worst recall/precision; single run.

description: On MedHallu (1,000 items), Jev scores 92.9% vs 95.1% GPT-5.6 and 92.4% Claude Haiku 4.5, at 2.6-6.5x the speed and 5-35x lower cost
data_and_n: MedHallu test split, 1,000 items; separate 1,000-item dev split for tuning
key_numbers: 92.9% Jev vs 95.1% GPT-5.6 Luna; AUROC 0.974; 99.5% accuracy on 37% highest-confidence items; 2.6-6.5x faster, 5-35x cheaper
notes: Preregistered (PREREGISTRATION.md); notes MedHallu answers are machine-generated and abstract-removed baseline still scores 66-83%, so task is not purely testing source-grounding.

description: Jev vs OpenAI structured outputs on 1,000 synthetic smoking-history extraction notes: complete-extraction accuracy 92.4% vs 98.7% for OpenAI, but Jev ~133x cheaper and ~5.2x lower mean latency
data_and_n: 1,000 synthetic outpatient progress notes
key_numbers: Complete-extraction accuracy 92.4% vs 98.7%; cost $0.18 vs $24.54 (1,000 notes); mean request time 0.405s vs 2.093s
notes: A candidate-selection comparison (both pick from a shared parser's candidates), not unconstrained generative extraction; single run per provider, no confidence intervals; dataset-generation code withheld.

description: Jev triages 150 synthetic prior-authorization requests: 0/47 clear-denial cases wrongly auto-approved; the sole miss flagged by its own low (0.24) confidence
data_and_n: 150 synthetic PA requests
key_numbers: p50 latency 362.5ms; cost $0.0049/150 requests; 0/47 unmet-criteria cases auto-approved; lowest-confidence decision (0.24) was the one borderline slip-through
notes: Synthetic data only, explicitly not clinically validated; urgency assessed independent of submitter's self-reported claim, disagreeing 19.3% of the time.

description: Jev vs GPT-5.6 Terra and three open Jev-shaped models on 5 classification tasks; Jev 0.897 accuracy on CLINC vs open-jev's 0.610, and Jev's latency stays flat from 2 to 151 options
data_and_n: 300 items per task x5 tasks (CLINC150, Banking77, SST-5, IMDB x2)
key_numbers: CLINC acc 0.897 vs 0.610 (open-jev); sentiment5 acc 0.570; clinc ECE 0.039; latency flat 0.17-0.20s across option counts
notes: n=300/task, differences under ~5pts are noise; training-data overlap confound flagged by the author.

description: Jev vs GLiNER2.5 zero-shot classifier on three BTZSC-derived datasets; Jev wins accuracy and Brier on AG News/Banking77 but is much worse-calibrated on DAIR Emotion
data_and_n: 300 examples (100 per condition): AG News, Banking77/BTZSC, DAIR Emotion
key_numbers: AG News acc 0.910 vs 0.700; Banking77 0.870 vs 0.610; Emotion 0.480 vs 0.440, Brier 0.846 vs 0.668, 16% zero-probability-on-truth
notes: Explicitly a 300-example pilot, not a leaderboard; public data may be in either model's training set.

description: LangGraph support-triage benchmark: Jev vs GPT-4o-mini behind an identical confidence gate; Jev is faster/cheaper/more accurate (87.5% vs 75%) but its confidence gate caught 0 of its 3 routing errors
data_and_n: 24 invented/labeled support tickets
key_numbers: Jev 163ms vs GPT 1,164ms to decision; 87.5% vs 75.0% department accuracy; $0.06 vs $0.37 per 1,000 tickets; confidence separation -0.010 (gate caught 0/3 errors)
notes: Explicitly states the 24-ticket sample is too small to establish calibration ("untested at adequate power, not refuted"); self-authored tickets, not from real traffic.

description: Compares Jev, open-weight Laya, and a frozen fly-connectome reservoir on 4 public decision tasks; Jev leads accuracy on 3 of 4 (up to 99.3%) but a 151-option intent menu made hosted Jev stop mid-run at 4,060/5,500 rows

notes: Author notes hosted Jev API stopped answering mid-benchmark (finishability issue); no single winner declared.

description: Feishu (Lark) Chinese message-classification benchmark, Jev vs open-weight Laya on 64 frozen synthetic scenarios; Jev scores 64/64 (100%) single-choice and 63/64 (98.44%) four-question-decomposed vs Laya's 20/64 (31.25%) and 18/64 (28.12%)
data_and_n: 64 synthetic Feishu-style Chinese scenarios (8 categories x 8); always-guess-one baseline 16/64 (25%)
key_numbers: single-choice Jev 64/64 (100%) vs Laya 20/64 (31.25%); four-question Jev 63/64 (98.44%) vs Laya 18/64 (28.12%); latency 253ms vs 151ms
notes: Explicitly synthetic/AI-assisted labels, no independent multi-annotator review; cloud (Jev) vs local MPS (Laya) latency not a same-hardware comparison.

description: One direct Jev question per row against 12 to 14 Jev-scored dimensions with fitted weights, 5,477 rows on three tasks: Japanese NLI 0.908 vs 0.837, but 25x more hard-benign false positives
Three small experiments on Japanese text: 10 to 12 of 12 correct on triage tasks, 12/14 on a guardrail set, matching GPT-5.6 at lower latency and cost
notes: Small sample sizes (12-14 items); first-hand implementation test by AI Native's CEO/PM.

description: Study testing whether jev-1.13.0's calibrated probability outputs give tradeable alpha in short-horizon BTC markets; on a 40,320-state holdout, adding Jev's probability to deterministic volatility features improved Brier by only 1.4e-05 - 'NO CURRENT ALPHA CANDIDATE'
data_and_n: 10,080 one-minute BTC timestamps (original run); 40,320-state independent holdout (2026-08-15 to 09-11)
key_numbers: holdout Brier 0.2131387, log loss 0.6187, ECE 0.0422; Jev+volatility improves Brier only 1.4058e-05 over volatility alone; classical breakout/volatility baselines also failed the 15bps cost model
author_type: researcher/academic (paper artifact; project was closed after negative results)
notes: Retrospective queries may overlap Jev's training data (not a prospective frozen deployment test); cost/slippage assumptions are approximations; BTC-focused, one-minute horizon only; negative/inconclusive results explicitly preserved.

description: Compares Jev against fine-tuned open-weight Laya across six public workflows and a chat-moderation study; Jev scores 80.0% vs Laya's fine-tuned 79.4% on Banking77 and catches 94.0% of harmful XSTest prompts vs Laya's 91.5%
data_and_n: Banking77 3,080 test/1,001 train; five public workflows; moderation 67,890 decisions across 27 model-task runs + 22,630 matched Jev decisions; XSTest 250 harmless prompts
model_version: Jev (unstated exact version) vs Laya (base and fine-tuned)
key_numbers: Banking77: Jev 80.0% vs Laya-FT 79.4%; prompt-injection: Jev 78.7% vs Laya-FT 94.8%; XSTest: Jev 94.0% harmful-catch/7.6% false-alarm vs Laya-FT 91.5%/47.2%
notes: Separates locally measured results from OpenAI/Mistral's own advertised scores; one training seed and shared-workstation timing limit generalization.

description: Pytest plugin using Jev as a semantic-assertion judge; on 12 designed test cases it gave the same verdicts as Claude Sonnet 5, 5x faster and 110x cheaper
data_and_n: 12 designed test cases (7 pass, 5 fail) x3 runs
key_numbers: Judging time 5.3s vs 27.1s (Sonnet 5); cost $0.00017 vs $0.0192; all three judges 12/12 in all 3 runs
notes: Author states this measures speed/cost/agreement on designed cases, not general accuracy; own model shifts 0.16-0.23 across repeat calls.

description: Claude Code safety-gate plugin using Jev to judge command/edit/MCP-call risk; measured on 268 shell commands, 32 edits, 30 MCP calls and 34 injection/benign texts: 0 dangerous actions auto-allowed, 17/17 injections flagged, plus a cited external Jev-vs-LLM head-to-head on real GitHub issues
data_and_n: 268 shell commands, 32 edits, 30 MCP calls, 34 injection/benign texts (held-out half roughly half of that); cited 500 VS Code issues
key_numbers: Held-out: 0/68 dangerous shell commands auto-allowed, 11/11 injections flagged, 0/13 benign texts flagged; cited Jev vs GPT-5.6 Luna 79.8% vs 78.6% Choice accuracy, CI [-1.4,+3.8]
notes: Labels are the plugin author's own on small held-out corpora (33-68 rows per category); explicitly notes Jev's probabilities move about +/-0.03 between identical calls (non-determinism affects deny/defer boundary).

description: About 16,000 real calls over two days on public and private data, asking whether Jev works better as a classifier or as a pre-filter

Financial-agent reliability harness comparing a Jev-first hybrid router/guardrail vs a pure LLM+DSPy pipeline on 50 stratified FinAgent tasks; Jev hybrid is 5.6x faster/12x cheaper at routing, 100% vs 75% on adversarial claim verification, and blocks injection/cross-client requests before any LLM call (3/50 hard-blocked)
data_and_n: FinAgent-133-derived, 50 stratified tasks per arm (synthetic/mock banking data)
key_numbers: routing 150ms/$0.001 (Jev) vs 842ms/$0.012 (DSPy); adversarial verification 100% vs 75%; injection probe 0.98 calibrated vs 60% bypassable prompt guard; 36/50 escalated from Jev to DSPy, 3 hard-blocked
notes: Explicitly synthetic/mock data throughout (no real banking data); reference prototype, not production; 50-row sample is small for the headline economics extrapolation.

description: Jev vs an LLM stand-in across four decision domains (CI triage, checkout fraud, dunning, PR review); Jev Brier 0.117/ECE 0.118 vs LLM's 0.274/0.337 on the checkout task
data_and_n: 24 decisions, 4 providers x4 domains x3 runs (144 records); synthetic calibration probe
key_numbers: checkout Brier 0.117/ECE 0.118 (Jev) vs 0.274/0.337 (llm); triage pass rate 50% (8/12); category never flipped in 30 repeat runs
notes: Self-labelled "learning project, not a benchmark," n=24 decisions, "treat every number as anecdote."

description: LLM-gateway guardrail built on Jev, evaluated as a prompt-injection classifier on 662 labeled prompts (deepset/prompt-injections); at threshold 0.1, precision 0.992/recall 0.890/F1 0.938, ROC-AUC 0.990, but the reliability table shows the model is under-confident (a 0.15 score is nearly always a true injection)
data_and_n: deepset/prompt-injections, 662 labeled prompts (263 injections, English+German)
key_numbers: F1 0.938 at threshold 0.1 (precision 0.992/recall 0.890); ROC-AUC 0.990; ECE 0.122, Brier 0.092; regex baseline F1 0.430; p50 latency 226ms, $0.017/1k requests
notes: One live run, cassette-replayed; only the injection question evaluated systematically (routing quality on live backends explicitly not measured).

description: Since the weights are fixed, tests prompt-side reweighting: 76.8% alone, 87.0% after a reweighting layer fit on 140 labels; a fine-tuned Laya reached 89.6%
notes: Improvement achieved via added diagnostic question/reweighting, not actual fine-tuning (Jev's weights aren't tunable).

description: Prompt-injection detection benchmark: Jev vs Claude Haiku, PromptGuard-2, and PIGuard on 11,900 labeled prompts from 4 public corpora; Jev has the best AUPRC (0.980) and least over-defense, but 3x worse calibration than Claude

model_version: Jev v1 and v2 (two question wordings), via OpenRouter/direct
key_numbers: Jev v2: catch 77.6%, panic rate 1.5%, ECE 0.058, AUPRC 0.980; Claude Haiku catch 86.7% but panic 6.2%, ECE 0.021; at 95% catch rate Jev v2 panic 16.5% vs Claude 52.2%
notes: Notes prompt wording alone moved the headline panic-rate figure by 28% between two Jev question variants; Claude occupies only 5/10 confidence bins (near-bimodal), flattering its ECE.

description: Eval of Jev on Spanish clinic phone-call triage (24 synthetic calls x4 questions); overall accuracy 84.4%, but confidence-gated accuracy is 98.6% on the 75% of answers with confidence >=0.80 vs only 41.7% on the rest
data_and_n: 24 synthetic Spanish clinic calls x 4 questions = 96 decisions, 9 deliberate trap cases
key_numbers: overall accuracy 84.4%; confidence>=0.80: 98.6% acc (71/72, 75% coverage) vs <0.80: 41.7% acc; cost $0.00083 for all 96 decisions
notes: Single-author-written cases/labels ("favours the model"); label-audit corrected 5 ground-truth errors; documents a specific failure mode (severe-problem reports miscoded as "angry customer").

description: Local playground demoing five production patterns for Jev; reports ad hoc measured latency (330ms-1.2s), cost ($0.042/M), sharp retrieval discrimination (0.970 vs <0.07 for distractors), and a documented "jaggedness" case where a better answer scored lower than a worse one
data_and_n: ad hoc, unspecified small samples (illustrative single-call examples, not a labeled dataset)

data_and_n: LLM-AggreFact/MiniCheck, 495 labeled claims (paired, identical items for both models)
key_numbers: balanced accuracy Jev 73.3 vs Astra 73.8 (diff -0.6, CI [-5.6,+4.5]); false-verification 23.2% vs 14.1%; cost $0.048 vs $8.93-10.70 per 1,000 claims
notes: Small per-dataset dev-split sample (45/dataset); an early prompt asymmetry favoring Jev was found and fixed before final runs; one Astra run discarded due to author's own token-budget bug.

description: Jev as a reranker vs Cohere/ZeroEntropy/DeepSeek/Qwen on 8 BEIR-style datasets; Jev's rubric nDCG@10 (0.692) statistically ties Cohere Pro (0.691) and beats it on negation pairs (71% vs 67%)
data_and_n: 1,617 scored questions across 8 datasets, +NevIR 1,383 pairs, +BRIGHT, +MIRACL French
key_numbers: nDCG 0.692 vs Cohere 0.691 (CI crosses zero); NevIR 71% vs Cohere 67%; Open-Jev 9B nDCG 0.600 vs BM25 0.486
notes: Exploratory paired bootstrap without multiple-comparison correction; reversing passage order changes Jev's top pick on 24.7% of queries vs 92.6% for a small Qwen baseline.

description: Jev tested as a RAG hallucination guard, reranker and retriever against IBM's STAIR and hybrid search; the only clear win was using Jev to decide when to retry a refused answer (78.0%->81.0% correct)
data_and_n: SQuAD 2.0 n=150 (50 unanswerable); SearchTome 518 retrieval + 200 answer questions
key_numbers: pairwise rerank 90.0% correct vs 87.3% baseline; ToC routing 39.2% R@1 vs hybrid 73.2%; retry-gate 78.0%->81.0%, refusals 17.5%->13.5%
notes: Small samples (150-518); "Jev as a guard" showed no effect, agreeing with all 8 remaining hallucination errors at confidence 0.82-1.0.

description: Jev used as a confidence/verification judge in a local-LLM RAG pipeline on 500 SimpleQA questions; Jev's confidence tracks passage relevance (AUROC 0.899) and ranks better than the small model judging itself (AUROC 0.926 vs 0.804), but the full judged pipeline scored 0.612 vs 0.740 for a no-judge baseline
data_and_n: SimpleQA, 500 questions (9,075 passages for informativeness check; 20-question pilot for the Gemma comparison)
key_numbers: passage-relevance AUROC 0.899 [0.881,0.916]; Jev vs Gemma AUROC 0.926 vs 0.804 (pilot, n=12 questions); end-to-end score 0.612 (judged) vs 0.740 (no-judge baseline), missing its main preregistered bar
notes: Answer-in-passage label is an approximate proxy (string match); Gemma-comparison finding rests on a small n=12-question/90-passage pilot; end-to-end pipeline explicitly did not beat the simpler baseline.

description: On 500 real book searches, Jev-based semantic matching hit 99.4% vs a regex heuristic's 96.0% (McNemar p~0.0005)
data_and_n: 500 YA novel search queries via Open Library's real search API (2026-09-20)
key_numbers: baseline 480/500 (96.0%) vs Jev 497/500 (99.4%); McNemar exact p~0.0005; discordant pairs Jev right 20, baseline right 3
notes: Hand-adjudicated ground truth; two of Jev's three losses were fixed post-hoc by a tie-break policy change (would raise Jev to 499/500 in-sample, but as-run 497 is reported as headline).

description: Jev (Noul) vs Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B as a production reranker on two BEIR datasets: rankings are statistically tied (nDCG@10 +0.022 on SciFact, not significant on NFCorpus, and non-replicating in 1 of 3 repeats), while Jev is ~2x faster/tighter-tailed and Qwen is ~4x cheaper
data_and_n: BEIR SciFact (300 queries) and NFCorpus (323 queries)
notes: Repeating the SciFact run twice more found the significant win fails to replicate in 1 of 3 repeats; both datasets are scientific/public (possible training overlap); rubric variants were first drafts, not held-out selected.

description: RAG passage filter/reranker built on Jev; SciFact NDCG@10 75.13 (Jev) vs 72.11 (Ettin) vs 66.47 (BM25), CRAG QA accuracy 42.5% vs 30% baseline at 56.8% higher API cost
data_and_n: SciFact 300 test queries; HotpotQA/MuSiQue 200 questions each; CRAG 40 test questions; ecosystem pilot over FiQA/NFCorpus/SciFact
model_version: Jev via TypeSafe API (jev-latest pinned per eval)
key_numbers: SciFact NDCG 75.13 vs 72.11/66.47; CRAG accuracy 42.5% vs 30%, +56.8% cost; HotpotQA F1 76.70->77.20 (CI includes zero)
notes: Several reported deltas' confidence intervals include zero; filtering sometimes increased wrong answers; author calls it "exploratory evidence, not a universal win."

description: Jev vs an NVIDIA cross-encoder vs no reranker in a RAG pipeline on XQuAD-EN/SciFact; Jev clearly beats no-reranker, statistically ties NVIDIA, and is well-calibrated enough (ECE 1.33%/6.25%) to filter at 94.9% precision for 5.1% coverage
data_and_n: XQuAD-EN 1,190 questions; SciFact 300 claims
model_version: TypeSafe Jev 1.13 via Vercel AI Gateway/OpenRouter
key_numbers: SciFact nDCG 79.29% (Jev) vs 78.70% (NVIDIA) vs 71.67% (none); ECE 1.33%/6.25%; answerability gating raises F1 30.6%->31.3% while skipping 9.8% of calls
notes: Decision-layer analyses (confidence partitioning, answerability gating) are explicitly labeled exploratory/post-hoc; all published runs cost $0 via free tiers.

description: Controlled Jev-vs-GPT passage reranking benchmark on 8 technical-manual questions; Jev found all required evidence on 5/6 vs GPT's 3/6, at roughly 18x lower cost
data_and_n: 8 author-created questions; 7,854 passages from PostgreSQL/Emacs/Emacs Lisp/RFC 9110 corpus
key_numbers: evidence-group recall 94.4% (Jev) vs 77.8% (GPT); cost $0.0188 vs $0.3417 for all 8 questions
notes: Small n (8 questions); evidence labels partly expanded after seeing results (not fully blind); "scores are not established as calibrated probabilities."

description: Jev used as a BEIR-shortlist reranker vs Cohere/Voyage/Mixedbread/LLM judges; Jev's per-document Noul scoring is at-or-above Cohere on all three corpora and trades with Voyage rerank-3 (the strongest specialist reranker) at a third of Cohere's price
data_and_n: BEIR shortlists: SciFact 300q, NFCorpus 323q, FiQA 300q (fixed BM25 top-30)
key_numbers: SciFact nDCG 0.772 (Jev, per-pair) vs 0.755 (Voyage) vs 0.745 (Cohere); calibration: docs scored>=0.9 relevant 76% of the time, <0.1 relevant 0.5% of the time
notes: Full determinism/position-bias/calibration checks are detailed in a linked RESULTS.md; Jev untuned per-corpus, domain-neutral phrasing.

description: 200-row BigQuery pilot shows Jev matches or slightly trails Gemini 2.5/3.1 on Stack Overflow tag classification while being faster and cheaper than Gemini 3.1 Pro
data_and_n: BigQuery public Stack Overflow posts_questions, 200-row pilot (10 per tag x 20 tags)
key_numbers: Jev 86.5% (173/200) at 368ms p50 and /bin/bash.009/200; Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite 86.0%; Gemini 3.1 Pro 87.0% at 4,807ms and /bin/bash.551/200
notes: Author states this is a 200-row pilot, 'not a general model ranking'; costs exclude infra overhead.

description: Obsidian search plugin using Jev as a two-stage BM25+AI reranker; across a 120-live-query benchmark, adding Jev reranking lifted nDCG@10 from 0.5258 to 0.8788 (+67%) at ~750ms round-trip and ~$0.00003/query, with exact-expression recall@50 improving from 95.8% to 100%
data_and_n: 120 live queries (public corpus); 10,000-note stress test for indexing
key_numbers: nDCG@10 0.5258 (BM25) -> 0.8788 (+Jev); recall@50 95.8% -> 100.0%; Katakana/loanword recall@5 46.3% -> 61.0%; live API latency 747ms; cost $0.000028/request
notes: README methodology is summarized with marketing framing ('empirically proven', 'revolutionary'); detailed method is in linked docs (docs/benchmark/) not reproduced in full here; product is a development preview (v0.1.0).

description: Jev-assisted reranking of Nevada statute search vs keyword search on 200 natural-language legal questions; top-5 hit rate rose from 37.5% to 60.0%
data_and_n: 835 NRS chapters; 200-question natural-language study; 598 query events, 904 Jev ranking arms
notes: Independent legal-relevance review pending; nominated hits are not confirmed legal accuracy; self-run, not externally audited.

description: Claims judged against provided passages on the author's structured QA set; about 90% correct
BM25 + Jev calibrated reranking CLI scores 0.900 any-gold@10 on SWE-bench Lite file localization and beats published BM25/cross-encoder baselines on BEIR
data_and_n: SWE-bench Lite; BEIR (details in docs/BENCHMARKS.md)
key_numbers: 0.900 any-gold@10 (SWE-bench Lite); beats published BM25 and cross-encoder baselines on BEIR; ~2s and ~$0.01/cold query
notes: Author states it does not reach the 'LLM-reranker frontier'; full tables in docs/BENCHMARKS.md (not fetched).

description: Jev as a per-candidate relevance filter vs an LLM judge in retrieval: Recall@20 0.118 vs 0.129, nDCG@20 0.217 vs 0.235, at near-equal cost (about $0.7 each) because Jev makes 20x the calls at 1/19 the price

notes: recall ceiling reported

description: CLERC legal search: Jev reranking lifts BM25 top-1 from 5% to 18% and top-10 from 38% to 62%; 11 of 13 answers had zero variance across 5 repeats

description: Jev-reranked file retrieval lifts SWE-bench-style recall@1 from 0.25 to 0.74 and cuts coding-agent tool calls 16-25%, at equal resolve rate
data_and_n: 20 SWE-bench Verified django tasks + 13 unfamiliar-repo tasks (2 model backends); 20-task retrieval sweep over ~2,000-file corpus
key_numbers: recall@1 0.25->0.74, recall@10 0.74->0.96; tool calls -16% to -25%; resolve rate unchanged (15/20 vs 14/20; 4/13 vs 4/13)

description: 33,047 catalogue entries and 164 real queries: Jev reranking measured against the existing pipeline, with cases where it hurt

Search stopping, coding-memory reranking and multi-hop relation selection in three RAG systems; a companion page covers 2,172 Chinese queries and their English translations against BGE-M3 and Voyage rerank-3

Graded relevance eval of a Jev score-rerank vs embedding search on 9,831 labeled (query, skill) pairs: standalone Jev rerank does not beat bge-m3 embeddings, but fused with embeddings it becomes the best system, and that survives a judge-bias control
data_and_n: 164 queries, 9,831 labeled (query, skill) pairs
key_numbers: rrf(bge-m3,jev) 0.864 NDCG@10 vs bge-m3 alone 0.774; jev-score(bge-m3) 0.785; standalone Jev rerank vs bge-m3 is +0.012 under merged labels but -0.028 under LLM-only labels
notes: Careful judge-circularity control (own Jev labels vs independent Claude-Haiku labels vs 30-pair hand adjudication, quadratic-weighted kappa 0.71); concludes Jev is useful only as a fused second signal, not standalone.

description: Jev vs an LLM-judge guardrail inside a multi-agent customer-service assistant, on 51 labelled scope cases: tied accuracy (94% vs 90%), 27x faster and 47x cheaper at full 25-rule coverage, with far better-separated confidence (0.44-1.00 vs 0.96-0.99)

key_numbers: accuracy 48/51 vs 46/51; coverage-matched cost $125 vs $5,880 per 1M reviews; confidence range 0.44-1.00 vs 0.96-0.99

description: Jev-based network intrusion detector vs an LLM and a Random Forest on NSL-KDD; Jev is 4.8x faster, 3.8x cheaper, and catches 1.5x more zero-day attacks than the LLM

notes: Explicitly pilot numbers pending a disjoint 'paper' split; notes the gateway masked Jev's version during the pilot and Jev noul answers carry no confidence field.

description: Evaluates Jev as a content-safety classifier on six public benchmarks (HateCheck, ToxicChat, Aegis v1/v2, WildGuardTest, HarmBench), comparing measured F1 against Mistral Shieldstral's announced numbers

key_numbers: hatecheck 99.23%; toxicchat 75.72% (Shieldstral 84.1, -8.38pp); aegis_v2 unsafe-prompt 83.57% (-2.63pp); harmbench harmful-request 99.16% (-0.24pp); latency p50/p95 493.8/661.2ms
notes: WildGuardTest response tasks NOT-ASSESSABLE due to gated-download limits; Shieldstral deltas are aggregate-only, no paired test possible.

description: Compares Jev, GPT-5.6 Terra and Claude Opus on a 100-case synthetic vulnerability-triage corpus (injection/broken-access-control/SSRF); latest recorded run: 1,500 decisions across all three models

key_numbers: 1,500 decisions, 0 errors, corpus label-neutral by construction; per-model balanced accuracy shown on the linked dashboard
notes: Explicitly 'a descriptive, synthetic demo-not a statistically powered benchmark'; earlier runs (v2-v4) were superseded for label leakage.

description: Two Jev-based safety/PII detectors (halo, prism) validated on synthetic held-out corpora; halo reports 100% recall, 0% disruptive false-positive rate, 98-100% category accuracy

key_numbers: recall 100%, disruptive FPR 0%, category accuracy 98-100%, ~390ms p50, ~$0.00026/call
notes: README states these are 'development benchmarks on synthetic data, not production-accuracy claims.'

description: Jev as a single yes/no judgment detecting real secrets in code/config snippets, 100 balanced cases: 99% accuracy; a harder config-only batch (no vendor prefix, low entropy) drops to 15-16/20
data_and_n: 100 main cases; 17 edge cases; 20 config-shaped cases
key_numbers: 99/100 main; 16/17 edge; 15-16/20 config batch, AUC 0.939/0.955
notes: All secret values are synthetic/never valid; config batch deliberately built to defeat entropy/vendor-prefix heuristics, which is exactly where accuracy drops.

description: Streaming secret-leak guardrail: Jev matches Claude Haiku/Opus on 5/5 detection at ~308ms vs 1,554-2,746ms, with zero token leakage across engines
data_and_n: 5 attack scenarios x 3 engines; 400-token synthetic response for cost benchmark
key_numbers: 308ms p50 (Jev) vs 1,554-2,746ms (Claude); 0/5 leaked across engines; naive vs batched: 56,278 vs 6,726 chars sent
notes: Explicitly states false-positive rate is unmeasured ("five scenarios are not an eval set"); finds Claude Opus 5 sometimes refuses to evaluate harmful content, a guardrail failure mode not seen with Jev or Haiku.

description: Jev 1.13 vs GPT-5.6 Luna triaging 100 labeled phishing/safe emails; accuracy is a statistical tie (81% vs 78%) but Jev is ~6x faster and ~4x cheaper per email
data_and_n: 100 labeled emails (50 phishing/50 safe) from an 18.6k-email public dataset, balanced sample seed=42
key_numbers: accuracy 81% vs 78%; recall 66% vs 58%; false alarms 4% vs 2%; time/email 0.42s vs 2.63s; cost/1000 emails $0.04 vs $0.16
notes: Author calls it 'a pilot, not a benchmark' - single run, older public dataset, no threshold tuning/ROC AUC.

description: 34-case labeled support-triage benchmark for Jev 1.13 across noul/choice/score questions, plus a local Laya comparison; noul urgency 78.6% accuracy, choice/department 100%, run-to-run consistency mean |dp|=0.004
data_and_n: 34 cases (4 composite, 5 Turkish); Laya comparison on 30 English cases
key_numbers: noul accuracy 0.786@0.5 (0.917 clear cases); choice 1.000 (14/14); consistency mean|dp|=0.004, max 0.04, 0 decision flips; Laya noul 0.833 vs Jev 0.750; Laya choice 0.750 vs Jev 1.000
notes: Small n (34-38 cases); Turkish cases show no accuracy degradation.

description: MCP bulk-decision tool sending records to Jev for triage; measured on real UX-feedback and GitHub-issue triage tasks, cutting total agent cost 32.8-77.3% while accuracy with human review moved from 84.2% to 90.2% (mini) but fell on Luna-routed OpenCV issues
data_and_n: 1,000 UX reviews (GPT-4.1 mini and Luna reviewers); 300 OpenCV issues (GPT-4.1 mini and Luna reviewers)

key_numbers: UX mini cost -48.9%, accuracy 84.2%->90.2% (+4 to +8pp 95% CI); OpenCV mini cost -77.3%, accuracy 68.0%->74.7% (recall -5pp); Luna both cases lost recall
notes: Author stresses these are "guided API loops," not native Codex/Claude sessions or optimized baselines; full per-prediction audit trail published alongside stats.

description: 100 support tickets x4 questions through Jev vs Claude Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 Sol and Gemini 3.8 Flash; Jev costs 31-65x less and is 4-7x faster with accuracy within a few points of the others (93% routing, 99% refund, 89% sentiment)

key_numbers: total cost $0.0031 (Jev) vs $0.0960-$0.1990 (others); median latency 474ms vs 1937-3459ms; routing 93% vs 88-94%; text models agree with each other only 60-72% of the time
notes: 'Accuracy' is graded leave-one-out against the other models' majority answer, not ground truth, since the text models frequently disagree with each other.

description: Three small cookbook demos: parallel vs sequential Noul calls gave identical results at ~4.5-5x speedup; Choice correctly split 2 true/4 wrong/1 fabricated claims; Score ranked passive-aggressive notes correctly

key_numbers: ~4.5-5x speedup parallel vs sequential with identical results; 8/8 claims correctly classified; highest-scored note 2.95/3 at 0.95 confidence
notes: Tiny, hand-picked demo datasets (n=8-16), not a rigorous benchmark; author frames results as "what we found" rather than formal metrics.

description: Jev used as an LLM-judge, benchmarked head-to-head against GPT-4o, GPT-5.6-terra and a local Gemma judge on 14 frozen customer-support replies (28 runs each); Jev scores within 1.1pp of GPT-4o (67.2% vs 66.1%) while being ~11x faster (0.148s vs 1.658s)

key_numbers: llm_judge pass rate: Jev 67.2%, gpt-4o 66.1%, gpt-5.6-terra 65.2%, local gemma 79.5% (outlier); Jev latency 0.148s vs gpt-4o 1.658s vs local 13.7s
notes: No human oracle (measures inter-judge agreement, not ground-truth accuracy); n=14 single domain; rubric not held constant between Jev (Score criteria) and text judges (free-text prompt).

description: Jev vs GPT-5.6 Luna vs Claude Sonnet 5 on 30 hand-labeled support tickets (department/urgency/anger); Jev ties Sonnet 5 on full-correctness (25/30) while Luna is most accurate (28/30); Jev is 2.6-3.5x faster and 4-75x cheaper
data_and_n: 30 hand-labeled support tickets, 3 questions each (90 decisions)
key_numbers: all-3-correct: Jev 25/30, Luna 28/30, Sonnet5 25/30; median latency 575ms vs 1472ms vs 2002ms; cost $0.022 vs $0.088 vs $1.660 per 1k tickets
notes: n=30, one run, labels by a single author ("a small sanity check, not a benchmark leaderboard"); documents a specific failure mode -- Jev rates calm outage reports as "angry."

description: Repeatable classifier workbench measuring Jev accuracy on a fixed BANKING77 subset (77.9% accuracy, 76.4% macro F1 on 308 cases) via OpenRouter, plus small Jev vs Laya comparisons via classifier.dev (20/20 vs 19/20)

description: Jev as a pre-generation model router and post-generation code-change judge (accept/revise/escalate/block) across LiveCodeBench/SWE-bench pilots; the router matched always-using-the-expensive-model quality at 12.9% lower cost, while Jev's code judge caught 100% of unsafe changes but accepted only 28.6% of valid ones

description: Exploratory test of a Jev-based memory-context router: correct category selection in 23/24 cases and correct closed-choice probes in 22/22

description: Threshold-measurement tool (Janus) routing Jev vs a fallback LLM; on Banking77 (n=500) routing at a measured threshold beat either single model alone (80.2% vs 77.8%/78.8%) at 53% lower cost, but on a second dataset no threshold beat the better single model

description: Three head-to-head lanes vs LLMs: Jev+fallback beats a frontier model's cost 70x on 77-way ticket triage (84.0% at $0.08/1k vs 86.7% at $5.70/1k), fits sub-300ms voice-agent latency where no tested LLM does, and wins cleanly on bulk review tagging ($29 vs $189-6,174 per 1M rows)
data_and_n: unstated per-lane sample sizes; 5,000 reviews for bulk tagging; 1,000 voice-agent turns

description: 100-question benchmark across sentiment, spam, bug severity, ticket routing and urgency: Jev scored 98/100 (98%) with 0.994 average confidence on choice tasks
