description: Jev 1.13 vs GPT-OSS-120B, Mercury 2.5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash on 500 BANKING77 intents; Jev scores 81.0% accuracy at 347ms/$0.068 per 1,000, cheapest and fastest but least accurate of the four
data_and_n: 500 held-out BANKING77 test + 50 dev + 200 threshold-selection + 50 timing repeats/model = 3,200 attempts; follow-up 500 fresh cases
key_numbers: Jev 405/500 (81.0%) @347ms/$0.068 per 1k vs Gemini 427/500 (85.4%)@1489ms/$0.685; follow-up cascade 424/500 vs Gemini baseline 425/500, ~23.3% cheaper
notes: Draft technical report (not peer-reviewed); single dataset/host/date/label order, training contamination possible; audit fixes documented in ANALYSIS-AUDIT.md.

description: Real-time UI comparing Jev vs DeepSeek on identical comment batches; a 10,000-comment run scored by GPT-6 Astra shows Jev slightly behind DeepSeek on accuracy but 4x faster and cheaper
data_and_n: 10,000 comments (400 spot-checked)
key_numbers: Processing time 203.2s vs 823.5s; cost $0.84 vs $1.50; all-three-correct 62.69% vs 67.26%
notes: README explicitly notes this is an AI-assisted recheck, not a human gold standard; strict first-choice-only accuracy is lower (50.58%/55.45%). Chinese-language README.

description: 15-recipe cookbook applying Jev to real-world tasks (triage, tagging, search rerank, moderation, etc.), each with measured results on small hand-made datasets, e.g. search rerank 2/16->16/16 vs keyword search, moderation 0 false negatives/positives on 5 hazard types
data_and_n: 16-36 hand-made items per recipe, 13 core recipes + browser agent + Gmail case; ~425 calls total for recipes 1-13
key_numbers: search rerank 2/16 (keyword) -> 16/16 (Jev over 30 articles); multi-label tagging F1 87% @0.5; moderation 0 harmful posts published/0 false blocks; median latency 0.34-0.45s
notes: Author explicitly states "The scores show how each technique behaves; they are not benchmarks," due to small hand-made datasets.

description: Zero-shot Jev matches or beats trained spaCy and Claude Opus on spam/routing/Swedish-routing email classification tasks (e.g., 98.0% spam accuracy, 88.9% Swedish routing vs spaCy's 84.4%)
data_and_n: Enron-Spam 150+150; Bitext support routing 25/category x11; MASSIVE Swedish 20/scenario x18
key_numbers: spam: spaCy full-train 98.0% vs Jev 98.0%; routing: Jev 97.8% vs spaCy-20shot 94.2%; Swedish routing: Jev 88.9% vs spaCy full-train 84.4% vs Laya 54.4%
notes: Claude not run in this pass; category descriptions were tuned on the dev split before scoring test, so figures partly reflect prompt engineering.

description: Two benchmarks against Jev 1.13 via OpenRouter, including RAG reranking of 100 chunks on 350 frozen questions across 9 arms (2,800 calls, $1.36); arms answering under 90% of questions withheld, and a 46.5% retrieval ceiling published
data_and_n: 350 questions x 9 arms
key_numbers: 2,800 calls, $1.36; 46.5% ceiling
notes: Rankings disagree across arms

description: Adding Jev to rule-based data-sync error routing lifts exact accuracy from 26.7% to 88.3% on 60 synthetic held-out events, with zero incorrect assignments among the 44 cases rules couldn't decide
data_and_n: 60 synthetic held-out events (44 rules-unmatched)
key_numbers: exact accuracy 26.7% (rules) vs 88.3% (rules+Jev); macro F1 0.445 vs 0.889; Jev made 0 incorrect assignments on the 44 rules-unmatched cases
notes: Author stresses small n (102 synthetic events total), unvalidated labels (human_reviewed:false), not production accuracy.

description: Three provider paths (OpenAI Luna, DeepSeek Flash, Jev via Vercel Gateway) on the same five support-ticket threads; pairwise agreement tables per field, with the asymmetry of routing and protocols stated
data_and_n: 5 threads
notes: n=5; latency not controlled

description: Jev vs GPT-5 on a 1,000-item Banking77 sample: Jev alone 416/500 (32x cheaper), cascade 430/500 at 47.3% of GPT-5's cost
data_and_n: Banking77 (PolyAI), 1,000 sampled text-label pairs, scored on 500-item splits
notes: Author flags an earlier related naming experiment as having failed its controls; offline-reproducible from saved response fields.

description: 100-case synthetic benchmark: Jev vs GPT-5.6 and Claude Sonnet 5 on enterprise trade-surveillance routing; Claude beats Jev by 12.7pp on joint accuracy, but Jev has ~half the calibration error and is 7-13x faster and 75-151x cheaper
data_and_n: 100 synthetic cases x 3 repeats (300 case-repeats), 5 categories including adversarial/prompt-injection
key_numbers: Jev 47% [37-56%] vs Claude 60% [50-68%] vs GPT 57% [48-66%]; paired Claude-vs-Jev edge +12.7pp (p=0.019); Jev 0 false negatives on manual-routing cases vs 1 (Claude)/9 (GPT)
notes: Labels are unreviewed and written by one person (documented contestable case); explicitly "not evidence about any production workload."

description: Jev with retrieved in-context examples on BANKING77 (77-class intent), full 3,080-message test set: 92.40% accuracy vs 93.66% for a 2020 fine-tuned BERT specialist, for $0.44 total
data_and_n: 3,080 official test messages (BANKING77, CC-BY-4.0)
key_numbers: 92.40% (2,846/3,080) vs 93.66% BERT; macro-F1 0.9235; final-test cost $0.4375; mean latency 0.533s
notes: Benchmark-exposure/contamination cannot be ruled out; this is retrieval-augmented, not zero-shot; author reproduced the score independently and audited request logs.

description: Jev vs GPT-4o-mini structured-output on a 500-scenario synthetic triage dataset; live run shows Jev 5-6x lower p50/p99 latency, 99.60% department accuracy (ECE 0.0133) vs GPT-4o-mini's 100% at 4x the cost
data_and_n: 500 synthetic triage tickets
notes: Repo also ships a "simulated" mode whose numbers are fabricated by construction and explicitly not measurements -- only the "live" columns count.

description: Support-ticket routing benchmarks for Jev vs a keyword baseline across three versions; a v0.1.0 run scored Jev 16/16 department classifications vs keyword baseline 12/16, and a v0.3.0 challenge run matched 121/126 attempts on 42 agreed-reference cases
data_and_n: v0.1.0: 32 synthetic tickets (16 dev/16 test); v0.2.0: 48 frozen cases + 8 dev; v0.3.0: 48 harder synthetic cases
key_numbers: v0.1.0 Jev 16/16 vs keyword 12/16, p50/p95 latency 383/1,229ms; v0.3.0 121/126 matched on 42 agreed cases, 5 mismatches all went to review
notes: Author repeatedly cautions "this tiny synthetic result does not establish general accuracy, calibration, or production reliability"; only the second of two passes retained, so repeat consistency is not established.

description: Jev vs GPT-5.4/Sonnet 5/Gemini 3.1 Pro judging whether a citation supports a claim, 42 claims x5 repeated runs: on the hard 18 real claims Jev ties GPT-5.4 (73.3% vs 70.0% mean, not significant) at about 1/50th the cost
data_and_n: 42 claims (18 hard real, 24 easy constructed), 5 runs each
key_numbers: Hard-18 Jev 73.3% vs GPT-5.4 70.0% (p=1.000, not sig.); easy-24 Jev 91.7% vs frontier 100%; Jev ~$0.000025/claim vs GPT-5.4 $0.001289
notes: Exceptionally transparent, repeatedly retracting/correcting its own earlier headline claims (reasoning-arm gap, model pinning, decomposition, single-run overstatement) in the same README.

description: Same-split zero-shot Jev 1.13.0 vs frozen supervised checkpoints and a zero-shot NLI baseline on five NLP benchmarks; Jev trails supervised models by 2-15 points but beats zero-shot NLI by 13-27 points
key_numbers: BANKING77 Jev 79.90% vs supervised 94.77% vs zero-shot-NLI 67.14%; SST-2 Jev 94.50% vs supervised 96.44% (gap 1.95, CI includes zero)
notes: Paired 95% CIs reported; comparisons use identical instructions/label sets, so gap reflects zero-shot vs fine-tuned rather than prompt differences.

description: Jev as an LLM router: on LLMRouterBench's 13-model flagship pool a Jev-difficulty+retrieval router beats the best single model (62.4% vs 60.3% at lower cost), but an honest no-Jev ablation matches it exactly
data_and_n: LLMRouterBench eval half 5,835 queries (13-model pool); RouterArena pilot 100 cached queries
key_numbers: Router 62.4% vs best-single 60.3% (+2.1pt, 15% cheaper); no-Jev ablation also 62.4% (same frontier); pilot Jev-difficulty 69.5% vs GLiClass 69.1%
notes: Explicitly reports that the accuracy gain is driven by retrieval evidence, not Jev's difficulty signal, which was "largely redundant" on the main benchmark.

description: Intent classification (12 classes, n=3,447): Jev scores 0.9806 ROC-AUC/87.8% accuracy at 564ms, vs Gemini Flash Lite 0.9751/90.6% at 2,105ms, 26x cheaper
data_and_n: tanaos/synthetic-intent-classifier-dataset-v1, 11,489 rows (3,447 test)
key_numbers: ROC-AUC 0.9806; accuracy 87.84%; F1 0.879; 563.87ms mean latency; $0.006 total cost vs $0.158 for Gemini Flash Lite
notes: Jev has lowest accuracy/F1 of the four but by far the lowest cost and near-lowest latency; local models (LightGBM/DistilBERT) both faster and more accurate, showing a real capability/cost tradeoff.

description: LLM-routing proxy measures live Jev 1.13 feature latency vs local heuristics; same routing accuracy but p95 latency rose from 77.93ms to 490.38ms
data_and_n: bundled demo fixture (small, 'not research evidence' per README)
key_numbers: p95 latency 77.93ms (local) vs 490.38ms (Jev); same routes/accuracy
notes: Author explicitly says demo fixture is not research evidence; a full benchmark protocol is documented but not run at scale in this file.

description: Tests whether Jev-labelled customer-support tweets predict brand outage acknowledgements before companies announce them; at equal false-alarm budget Jev's "service-down x widespread" signal catches 1.7x more incidents (17 vs 10) with ~1.7h more lead time than raw tweet volume
data_and_n: 170,400 tweets to 7 brands (Oct-Nov 2017, Kaggle Customer Support on Twitter); 62 labeled incidents
key_numbers: AUC ~0.6 for all signals (not meaningfully separable); at 99th-pct threshold Jev catches 17/62 incidents (median 4.1h lead) vs volume 10/62; McNemar p=0.007 at 95th-pct threshold
notes: Author flags a built-in circularity (brands react to complaint volume) and multiple-comparisons caveat on the one significant p-value; total labeling cost $1.84.

description: Jev-based alignment verifier (sycophancy/deception/overreach) scores 94/94 (100%, Wilson CI 96.1-100%) on a labeled battery, with measured null-condition noise of sd 0.000-0.008 and zero verdict flips across identical/perturbed inputs
data_and_n: 94-case labeled battery; null-condition/invariance suite (n unstated exactly)
key_numbers: verdict+head accuracy 94/94 (100%), Wilson CI [96.1%, 100%]; null-condition noise sd 0.000-0.008/head, 0 verdict flips
notes: 'Calibration is against the Jev model' - must be re-derived if the underlying model changes; distinguishes measured properties from a marketing claim of 'guaranteed alignment.'

description: Jev-augmented decisions vs a production TF-IDF+Jaccard duplicate-thesis-title screener: 23/24 vs 8/24 correct, 0 vs 9 real duplicates missed, and 24/24 verdicts identical across 5 repeats
data_and_n: 20,000-title archive; 24 test cases (14 held out after the policy was frozen)
key_numbers: 23/24 vs 8/24 overall; hold-out split 13/14 vs 2/14; stability 24/24 identical over 120 repeat calls
notes: Ground truth was self-labelled by the author, not a librarian; identifies a real failure mode where Jev never sees candidates a leaky retriever drops.

description: On AG News (n=100), Jev matched Claude Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 at 87% accuracy each, while running 2.1-2.8x faster
data_and_n: AG News test set, 100 randomly sampled articles (seed=42), 4 categories
model_version: TypeSafe Jev (unstated version) via TypeSafe SDK
key_numbers: 87% accuracy all three models; Jev 0.80s vs 1.71s (Sonnet) vs 2.21s (Opus) avg latency; World category hardest (F1 0.81-0.84)
notes: Small sample (n=100); accuracy identical across all three models on this task, so the differentiator found is speed, not accuracy.

description: Jev vs GPT-5.2 as SUQL's semantic-verification backend on 94 independently-labeled predicate cases; Jev is ~37.5x cheaper and ~2.9x faster with a +2.1pt accuracy edge (94.7% vs 92.6%) that is not statistically significant (McNemar p=0.683)
data_and_n: 94 scoreable predicate cases (Yelp-grounded); 15 SUQL queries
key_numbers: accuracy 94.7% (Jev) vs 92.6% (GPT-5.2), F1 0.928 vs 0.896, not significant (p=0.683); cost $0.000084 vs $0.00315/call; p50 latency 394ms vs 1141ms; query-level exact-row-set match 11/15 vs 10/15
notes: n=94 small sample with wide CIs; reference labels from independent LLM annotation, not human annotators; explicitly does not claim equivalence or a Jev win; SUQL/OpenRouter Decisions API was alpha-stage at time of writing.

description: Local benchmark of Jev vs the open Laya-mlx model classifying 100 GitHub issues for beginner-friendliness, CV fit and difficulty; Laya is marginally faster and the two models agree only 42-80% depending on the field
data_and_n: 100 issues
key_numbers: mean latency 328.1ms (Jev) vs 309.2ms (Laya); agreement 80% (beginner-friendliness), 42% (CV fit), 61% (difficulty)
notes: Explicitly "a local benchmark experiment, not a production performance claim"; Jev was not warmed before timing so latency is directional only.

description: On 1,000 real job postings, Jev's fraud-detection PR-AUC (0.276) barely beat the majority-class floor and was indistinguishable from a hosted LLM (0.282), far behind a fitted TF-IDF model (0.780)
data_and_n: Kaggle Real/Fake Job Posting Prediction, 1,000-row random sample (seed 0) of a 3,182-row test split
key_numbers: Jev accuracy 0.947, F1 0.312, PR-AUC 0.276, ECE 0.046; tfidf PR-AUC 0.780; repeat fetch gave accuracy 0.945/F1 0.286 (drift)
notes: With only 53 positives, zero-shot arms' confidence intervals overlap and are "inseparable"; explicitly notes Jev's row can drift between identical requests since it "runs on a shared service."

description: Fact-checking auditor using Jev as a blinded/grounded judge; on paired misleading/honest synthetic drafts it reaches 100% block/pass/precision/recall after tuning, up from 78-87% pre-tuning
data_and_n: 30 drafts (3 domains) main suite, 3 runs each; separate untuned retail-domain holdout
key_numbers: Misleading blocked 80%->100%; honest passed 87%->100%; omission precision 50%->100%; retail holdout: all misleading caught, 2/3 honest passed pre-fix
notes: Author states engine was tuned on the main suite ("measures fit, not generalization"); holdout run was then also tuned after exposing 2 flaws.

description: Jev vs Gemini 3.8 Flash labeling 1,000 Android app reviews (sentiment/topic/bug/churn); Jev 4.1x faster and 7.0x cheaper, sentiment-vs-star-rating rho 0.80 vs Gemini's 0.82
data_and_n: 1,000 Android app reviews (Hugging Face sealuzh/app_reviews, 17 apps)
key_numbers: 4.6s/$0.023 (Jev) vs 18.8s/$0.158 (Gemini); rho 0.803 vs 0.822; topic agreement 84.4%, bug-call agreement 92.6%
notes: One recorded run pair; "agreement is not accuracy" since no human ground truth for topic/bug labels.

description: CLI that sorts text by Jev-judged pairwise comparisons (Bradley-Terry); validated against the CommonLit readability scale (r=0.82 vs a 0.88 human-agreement ceiling) and FOMC statement hawkishness ranking
data_and_n: CommonLit corpus (300 excerpts sampled from 4,724); 95 FOMC opening statements 2011-2026
model_version: Jev (jsort tool, provider-agnostic; also tested against local DiffusionGemma/Laya)
key_numbers: Pearson r=0.824 vs a 0.88 ceiling; rank correlation with rate move +0.46; beats SMOG (r=0.661) and Flesch-Kincaid (r=0.598)
notes: Uses seeded comparisons and a split-half reliability check (0.96-0.98); first-position lean reported (-0.04 to -0.07); local-model comparison in a linked doc.

description: Jev vs GPT-5.6 Luna on 300 review classifications (5 fields x100 reviews x3 reps); Luna edges out Jev 97.13% vs 96.13% overall field accuracy, Jev much faster/cheaper
data_and_n: 100 reviews x3 repetitions x2 models = 602 attempts (synthetic fixture)
key_numbers: overall field accuracy Jev 96.13% vs Luna 97.13%; all-5-correct 88.33% vs 90.67%; Jev 1 API error of 300
notes: Small synthetic dataset explicitly called 'one diagnostic run, not evidence of a general model ranking.'

description: Jev classifies style-guide exceptions across 256 Vale alerts/108 human-reviewed items; retained 7/7 known findings, suppressed 4/5 acceptable cases
data_and_n: 256 Vale alerts, 108-item human review set, 31 semantic findings on 27 real docs pages
key_numbers: 7/7 human-labeled findings retained; 4/5 acceptable cases suppressed, 3 sent to review; batching measured 12.2x cheaper/10x faster
notes: Numbers are partly summarized in README prose across many linked sub-reports rather than one master table; human labels used as ground truth.

description: 520 real social posts through four Noul pre-publish checks, compared with Claude Fable on agreement and cost
Applied survey QC on 6,019 respondents: Jev caught 38 bad respondents no rule-based check could see, for $0.32 total
data_and_n: 6,019 real survey respondents (foldable smartphone consumer survey)
key_numbers: 92.8% PASS / 3.6% REVIEW / 3.6% FAIL; +38 catches beyond rules; $0.32 total cost, 92s wall time
notes: No ground-truth labels for correctness; findings are qualitative; acknowledges Jev's English-first training vs Singlish text in the data.

description: Benchmarks Jev and a fine-tuned ModernBERT (Laya) against production LLM news-classification labels; Jev 86-94% match, Laya 93-97%, Gemini arbitration preferred Laya 75% of the time
data_and_n: production audit data, unspecified live-batch counts; Laya trained on 35,138/6,200 train/val sequences
model_version: jev-latest / typesafe/jev-1.13 via TypeSafe and OpenRouter
key_numbers: Jev tag/sentiment/validation match 94.2%/88.5%/86.1%; Laya 96.8%/95.4%/93.4%; cost savings 80-88% (Jev) vs >99.5% (Laya); Gemini arbitration 75% preference for Laya
notes: Feasibility rig, not production; Jev-LLM agreement is not agreement with human truth; author states human-reviewed samples still required.

description: Jev's zero-shot "will this repo gain stars" question ranks 1,132 new repos better (Spearman rho 0.435) than any trained day-one metadata model (rho 0.24)
data_and_n: 1,132 GitHub repos (retrospective proxy study), 5-fold CV with ~900 training labels per fold
key_numbers: Jev zero-shot rho 0.435 vs rho 0.24 trained-metadata baseline; ~100-200 labeled repos needed for a trained model to match it; total cost $0.085 for 1,132 repos
notes: Explicitly caveated as directional not a verdict -- no star count at entry (baseline missing), README text possibly reflects popularity rather than day-one state, possible training data leakage for the Jev model version used.

description: JevBench: an open, model-agnostic evaluation harness for typed decision models (Choice/Score/Noul) in the spirit of Jev, scoring any model family (LLMs prompted or as option-scorers, cross-encoders/rerankers, embedders, custom) with the right metric per question; dataset released separately, plus an add-on relevance task family.
data_and_n: 232-example gold sample (reliability=='gold'); ~46-row subjective-score subset for ordinal metrics; task taxonomy across type x context
model_version: jev (reference) plus Opus 5, GPT-5.5, GPT-6, gpt-oss-20b, bge-reranker, laya, bart-mnli, MiniLM
key_numbers: Jev overall 88.8% (choice 94 / noul 92), score-QWK 0.92 / MAE 0.20; top five (~88-91%) a statistical tie at n=232; only bge-reranker and option-scoring significantly mis-order
notes: General capability/leaderboard benchmark rather than a robustness-specific test; score-QWK tail is small (read as tiers); dataset shipped separately.
